subject: How to Input Data for multi species occupancy model in unmarked (unmarkedFrameOccuMulti)

messages.author: b18c7e3354ffe63c
messages.subject: How to Input Data for multi species occupancy model in unmarked (unmarkedFrameOccuMulti)
parts:
Dear all group members,
My apology for very basic question. But I cannot move forward without this basic idea.
I am trying to do multi species ( 4 species) occupancy model using "occuMulti" function with unmarked package. I do not know how to input data to run this model. Could anyone kindly suggest me how to input that kind of data type.

To use "unmarkedFrameOccuMulti", I found the example in Package ‘unmarked’ document:

S <- 3 # number of species
M <- 4 # number of sites
J <- 3 # number of visits
y <- list(matrix(rbinom(M*J,1,0.5),M,J), # species 1
              matrix(rbinom(M*J,1,0.5),M,J), # species 2
              matrix(rbinom(M*J,1,0.2),M,J)) # species 3  

I would like to know why use "list(matrix(rbinom(M*J,1,0.5),M,J)"?
It would be very grateful someone could explain me about it as well.

Thank you so much in advance,
Aye

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: How to Input Data for multi species occupancy model in unmarked (unmarkedFrameOccuMulti)
parts:
Aye,

For each species you should have a matrix in R with M rows (number of sites) and J columns (number of observations at each site), with each entry a 0 if that species was not detected and 1 if it was.
Then,  to make the input "y" you combine those matrices together in R into a list.

The code you asked about is generating simulated occupancy data to use as an example - that's what the rbinom() part is doing. I would suggest running the code you copied and looking at the resulting "y" in the R console to see how your own data should be structured.

Ken
